newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen shaky, small issues in lead.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen shaky, small issues in lead.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen in a shaky position on Thursday but could recover on the return of foreign buyers encouraged by the hot Thailand stock market.
Dealers said the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was vulnerable to the downside after breaking critical support at 1,970 points, but it could rebound in the short term.
On Wednesday, the STII closed 12.37 points lower at 1,968.91, with instituional demand confined to core stocks.
Volume was a modest 98 million shares, with the bulk of interest in small capitalisation and new stocks.
Dealers said they expected more punting in Malaysian issues from retail buyers hopeful of a spillover effect from Thailand.
Thailand decided on Wednesday to allow the baht to be floated with its value no longer set by a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
